title: Spectrum monitoring is not signals intelligence
abstract: Monitoring in a regulatory sense concerns spectrum use and compliance; military SIGINT concerns intelligence gained from signals. Shared radio physics does not merge their legal mandates or evidential goals.
limitation: Do not assume an allocation table describes actual transmissions, nor equate general-purpose sensors with military collection.

title: Australia: layered history from wartime origins to 1947
abstract: ASD provides a wartime chronology and separately describes the transition to a postwar organization. Treat institutional histories as primary evidence about published self-understanding, then seek independent archives for contested interpretations.
limitation: Do not infer what the organization can collect today from historical records.

title: French ROEM and cross-language terminology
abstract: Published French military sources use ROEM as electromagnetic-origin intelligence and situate it among several intelligence disciplines. Cross-reference foreign terms in their source language before translating to COMINT/ELINT categories.
limitation: A translation match is not proof that two countries use identical definitions or organizations.

title: The UK archive research strategy
abstract: HW series provide a document-retrieval approach to historical codebreaking; DEFE series provide a distinct defense-intelligence archival route. Oversight records provide public institutional context but not evidence of every historical activity.
limitation: Catalog existence does not establish the accuracy of the document contents.

title: Scholarly discovery is not copyright clearance
abstract: OpenAlex and Crossref provide searchable bibliographic metadata to discover and deduplicate works. Open-access visibility and CC0 metadata are distinct from permission to republish an author’s abstract or a complete paper.
limitation: Never batch-download full texts without checking each source’s license and site terms.

title: Provenance requires more than citations
abstract: Separate subject vocabulary (SKOS), catalog/resource metadata (DCAT), and claim-origin activity (PROV-O). Store original source IDs, review status, dated revisions and explicit source lineage to make agent retrieval auditable.
limitation: Formal vocabularies do not themselves guarantee factual truth.

title: Signals span multiple physical domains
abstract: RF telemetry, radar remote sensing and seismic waveforms rely on related sampling and inference principles but use different sensors, media, metadata and application constraints.
limitation: Do not treat a sensor taxonomy as a universal modulation or spectrum taxonomy.

title: Oversight is part of the technology story
abstract: Comparative public research should connect legal powers, independent review, rights protection and historical institutional explanations, rather than inventorying only equipment or national organizations.
limitation: An oversight framework is not proof that every decision has been legally correct.

title: Maxwell-to-information bridge
abstract: A number of current studies connect electromagnetic field models to communication and information-theoretic objectives. A shared vocabulary of assumptions may help flag invalid approximations across sources.
limitation: This is a synthesis proposal, not a demonstrated new physical effect.

title: Spectral resolution and adaptive observation
abstract: Time-frequency analysis involves resolution tradeoffs; adaptive windows and nonlinear sampling recovery are distinct responses to different assumptions.
limitation: No algorithm is universally better; compare reconstruction guarantees and benchmark conditions.

title: A science corpus is not yet an experimental result
abstract: ML RF papers can be linked by data modality, metrics, and evaluation protocol. Cross-paper leaderboard comparisons are invalid without common datasets and leakage controls.
limitation: Preprints and abstracts alone do not verify model generalization.

title: Document co-location and rights metadata
abstract: All publications should have one searchable local record, while full PDFs are mirrored only when rights allow; this avoids collapsing access into redistribution permission.
limitation: A checked license on a landing page does not imply every embedded figure is independently cleared.

title: Can versioned research packets reduce repeated parsing at unchanged answer quality?
abstract: Hypothesis: bounded, evidence-preserving source packets reduce repeated retrieval text if many research questions reuse overlapping source records.
limitation: Local packet payload experiment does not estimate real LLM inference cost, cache maintenance, retrieval relevance at scale, or latency under load.

title: Measurement metadata as a transferable scientific invariant
abstract: Candidate design insight: reproducibility across RF, astronomy and simulated signals depends on explicit sampling, calibration, transform, and provenance parameters.
limitation: Shared methodology, not a novel physical law; broad real-world validation and counterexamples remain to be investigated.

title: Provenance is part of the measurement
abstract: Across RF recordings, interferometric calibration and SAR products, the measurement must be interpreted together with acquisition context and signal transformations.
limitation: An architectural synthesis rather than a new physical law; requires formal cross-domain specification and tests.

title: Solar radio flux as an Atlas real-measurement pilot
abstract: A small 30-day NOAA sample can be analyzed offline to teach variability, measurement units and dated provenance without recording communications.
limitation: One month of observations cannot establish climatology, causal propagation effects or a new natural law.

title: Public national-intelligence evidence is not uniform
abstract: Countries publish different categories of institution records: doctrine, self-reports, oversight and historical pages. These should not be weighted as equal evidence of military technical operations.
limitation: Some sources concern civilian services, not military SIGINT; multinational comparison must retain source class.

title: Versioned packet provenance as a portable research contract
abstract: Recording metadata principles suggest an analogous packet contract where source identifiers, time scopes, hash manifests and inference status travel with a reusable summary.
limitation: Proposal for data engineering, not measured savings of inference tokens or a discovered physical principle.

title: Frequency stability is not measurement accuracy
abstract: Frequency accuracy, stability over a specified averaging interval, calibration traceability, and measurement uncertainty answer different questions. Report the observable, reference, interval, method, environmental conditions and uncertainty before comparing instruments.
limitation: A conceptual lab or service description is not a calibration certificate, and a small observed variation does not establish accuracy.

title: Public historical records have layered provenance
abstract: A finding aid, an agency history, a released document, and a historian's interpretation are distinct evidence objects. Record who created a document, which organization held or described it, its date and release context, then cite the specific item for event claims.
limitation: Publicly available collections are selective and incomplete; institutional histories describe the institution's account and cannot establish current capabilities.

title: Cross-scale observations need explicit joins
abstract: Daily solar-radio and geomagnetic products sit alongside one-minute solar-wind and GOES X-ray products. Their units, time supports, locations, processing, and sampling differ. A join requires a documented shared key and purpose; coincident timestamps alone do not establish common origin, propagation delay, causality, or forecasting power.
limitation: Bundled snapshots cover short and non-matching windows. The GOES pair is a structural two-channel join, not multi-instrument event attribution.
